fields.sample_size: 33 semi-structured interviews with 37 informants (utility directors, finance and customer-service staff, other municipal employees, water-commission members and elected officials) in 11 publicly owned water utilities (cities) in Massachusetts and Pennsylvania, 2020-2022, by Zoom; purposive sampling then snowball; one Pennsylvania city could not be recruited; Boston and Philadelphia are focal cities and the others are comparison cities matched on population, racial and ethnic composition and poverty
fields.effect_measure: qualitative typology (three 'value camps') of 11 utilities; no quantitative estimate
fields.effect_estimate: Utilities fell into three camps: Traditionalists (strict cost recovery; uniform rates seen as fair), Balancers (aware of affordability problems but held back by conformity, tradition and fiscal security) and Benevolence-Led (affordability in the mission, customer assistance programmes paired with outreach). Seven of the 11 utilities use ascending block rates; consultant-led rate studies benchmark against peers; conservation pricing and treatment upgrades are framed as costs to recover through uniform rates, reproducing distributive inequity, and procedural justice is largely absent. The authors argue that policies naming affordability as an objective, institutionalising participation and pairing ecological mandates with affordability funding could move Balancers toward benevolence-led practice. No data on assistance enrolment, shutoffs or household outcomes (the authors name this as a measurement gap).
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: CASP Qualitative per-item (re-appraised 2026-10-09 on the full text; supersedes the abstract-only rating): 1(aims)=Yes; 2(qual approach)=Yes; 3(design)=Yes (multi-site comparative design with cities matched on population, composition and poverty); 4(recruitment)=Yes (purposive and snowball sampling of rate-setting knowledge holders; one city not recruited, disclosed); 5(data collection)=Yes (semi-structured interviews by Zoom, transcribed verbatim); 6(researcher-participant)=Can't tell (not discussed); 7(ethics)=Yes (Northeastern University IRB, exempt, protocol 20-03-12; identifiers removed); 8(analysis rigor)=Can't tell (hybrid inductive-deductive coding in Dedoose with a codebook, but coder numbers and handling of contradictory data are not reported); 9(findings)=Yes (typology with quotations; limitations stated); 10(value)=Yes. Per CASP's own guidance no composite score is computed.

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative interview study of organisational values in 11 US municipal water utilities (33 interviews, 37 informants, Massachusetts and Pennsylvania); no estimate of access or affordability outcomes; read in full text 2026-10-09.
pdf_note: journal article PDF (Environmental Sociology, online 2 May 2026, doi 10.1080/23251042.2026.2666400), read as text in Drive file 23251042.2026.2666400.pdf
notes: Interview numbers (33 interviews, 37 informants, 11 cities) now recorded. The outcome is organisational values and policy design, not measured household access, so criterion 4 rests on affordability policy design.
